passage: Dhruv, your Joseph Uncle once hid a marksheet under a mattress. I was seventeen and had failed physics. Twenty-eight out of a hundred. I told myself I would fix it quietly: study hard, sit the re-exam, show Papa a pass. But the re-exam form needed the marksheet and a parent's signature, and the last date slid past while I told myself "tomorrow." Every dinner my stomach twisted. Then the school sent a letter about the missed form, and Papa read it at the table. He did not shout. He said, "You let me find out from a letter." That is what I remember, not the marks, but that sentence. It took a year before I felt he trusted me again.

qa.q: Where did Joseph hide the marksheet?
qa.a: Joseph hid it under a mattress.

qa.q: How did Joseph feel every dinner while hiding the result?
qa.a: Joseph felt anxious and fearful, shown by the stomach twisting, as the secret grew heavier each day.

qa.q: What choice in the story could have saved the re-exam, and how?
qa.a: Joseph could have shown the marksheet and asked for the signature before the last date, because the form needed a parent's signature and time was passing.

qa.q: How did Papa feel on reading the letter?
qa.a: Papa felt hurt more than angry, since it was the discovery by letter, and not the marks, that he spoke about.

grounding: The student conceals the marksheet and hopes to fix things quietly, but the secrecy adds fear, delays practical steps such as re-exam applications and damages trust when the truth emerges.

passage:
The marksheet came on Friday, and the maths line said 22 out of 80. Aparna folded it into eighths and hid it inside her geography atlas. Her parents were away at a wedding in Jaipur till Tuesday. She had four days.

She told her cousin Deepak on the phone, "I'll fix it quietly. I'll pass the re-test and they'll never know."

But she didn't know when the re-test forms were due, and she couldn't ask the teacher without the teacher asking about her parents. Every night she lay awake thinking about the atlas on the shelf.

On Wednesday, her father found a school notice in her bag: re-test applications, last date Monday, parent's signature required. The date had passed two days ago.

He didn't shout. He just looked at her and said, "Why didn't you tell me?" That hurt more than shouting.

qa.q: Where did Aparna hide the marksheet?
How did Aparna feel during the days she hid the result?
qa.a: She felt anxious and trapped, lying awake every night with the secret.

qa.q: What would you advise Aparna to do next?
qa.a: Tell her father everything now and ask the school together whether a late re-test application is possible, since hiding it has already cost time.

qa.q: How might her father have felt finding the expired notice?
qa.a: He likely felt hurt and let down, more by the secrecy than the marks, which is why he asked why she hadn't told him.

grounding: Shows a student hiding a marksheet to fix things quietly, with the secrecy adding fear, delaying the re-exam application and damaging trust when the truth emerges.

passage:
In their Pune housing society, Mridul was known as the boy who always topped. So when his Class 11 chemistry result came back as a fail, he put the report card in his school bag's inner pocket and told his parents the results were "delayed".

His best friend Madhav, from the next building, found out when they were walking to tuition. "You have to tell them."

"I'll just clear the re-exam first. Then I'll tell them it went fine."

For three weeks Mridul barely slept. He jumped every time the landline rang. He couldn't ask his teacher about re-exam forms without a parent signature, so he didn't ask.

Then his mother met his class teacher at the society Ganpati function. The teacher mentioned the re-exam deadline, and that Mridul's form was missing.

At home, his mother held out her hand for the report card. Her voice was quiet. "Three weeks, Mridul. You lied to us for three weeks."

qa.q: What excuse did Mridul give his parents about the results?
qa.a: He told them the results were "delayed".

qa.q: How did Mridul feel during the three weeks of hiding the result?
qa.a: He felt anxious and on edge, barely sleeping and jumping every time the landline rang.

qa.q: What could Mridul have done differently on the day the result came?
qa.a: He could have told his parents with a plan for the re-exam, so they could sign the form in time and help rather than find out from the teacher.

qa.q: How might Mridul's mother have felt hearing about the missing form from the teacher?
qa.a: She likely felt shocked, embarrassed and hurt, more by three weeks of lying than by the failed exam.

grounding: Shows a student hiding a failed result, with the secrecy adding fear, delaying the re-exam form and damaging trust when a parent finds out.
